title: 7-Day South Albania Road Trip: Summer Route Guide
excerpt: Plan your perfect 7-day South Albania road trip from Tirana Airport. Discover driving times, route tips, and top stops like Berat, Himarë, and Gjirokastër.
intro: Landing at Tirana Rinas (TIA) Airport is the gateway to one of Europe's most spectacular coastal and historical journeys. Southern Albania packs UNESCO world heritage sites, dramatic mountain passes, and turquoise beaches into a surprisingly compact region. Renting a reliable vehicle directly upon arrival at Tirana Rinas (TIA) airport from a provider like AutoConnect Rental ensures a seamless start to your self-drive journey down the coast. This curated guide helps you maximize your week on the road, ensuring you spend less time navigating and more time exploring.

sections.title: Planning Your 7-Day South Albania Road Trip
sections.body: To make the most of a 7-day South Albania road trip, a loop route is highly recommended. This route balances coastal beauty with rich inland history while keeping average daily drives under 2.5 hours. Your journey begins with an easy drive south before climbing over the dramatic coastal mountains and returning through the historical valleys. Starting directly from Tirana Airport allows you to bypass the heavy city traffic of central Tirana, setting a relaxed tone for the week ahead. Ensure your rental car is well-suited for both highway cruising and winding mountain passes.

sections.title: Day 1 to 3: From Tirana Airport to Berat and Himarë
sections.body: The drive from Tirana Airport to the UNESCO World Heritage city of Berat takes approximately 2 hours, covering around 120 km of well-paved roads. Spend your first night exploring Berat's famous white Ottoman houses. On Day 2, head toward the coast. Navigating the iconic Llogara Pass offers spectacular views of the Ionian Sea but features steep winding roads that require careful and attentive driving. Descend into the Albanian Riviera to reach Himarë, a relaxed coastal town where you can spend the night listening to the waves and enjoying fresh local seafood.

sections.title: Day 4 & 5: Sun and History in Sarandë and Ksamil
sections.body: Continue south from Himarë along the scenic coastal highway to the bustling hub of Sarandë/Saranda. Two nights in the Ksamil or Sarandë/Saranda area are highly recommended to allow for a full day of relaxation on the beaches and a visit to the nearby Butrint National Park. Butrint is a vast archaeological site where ancient Greek, Roman, and Byzantine ruins sit nestled within a lush wetland forest. Spending an extra day here gives you the flexibility to sunbathe on the white sands of Ksamil without rushing your cultural sightseeing.

sections.title: Day 6 & 7: The Stone City of Gjirokastër and Return
sections.body: Turn inland on Day 6 toward Gjirokastër, often called the 'City of a Thousand Steps'. This UNESCO-protected town features striking Ottoman-era tower houses climbing up the steep hillside. Walk up to the imposing Gjirokastër Castle for panoramic views of the Drino Valley. On Day 7, make the drive back to Tirana Airport. The return journey takes about 3.5 hours on comfortable national highways, allowing you to easily catch your evening flight home while reflecting on an unforgettable week of Albanian landscapes.

tip.title: Footwear for Historical Streets
tip.body: Sturdy footwear is highly recommended when visiting the steep, slick cobblestone streets of Gjirokastër and its historic castle. The centuries-old stones have been polished smooth by time and can be surprisingly slippery, even during dry summer days.

faq.question: Is 7 days enough to see Southern Albania by car?
faq.answer: Yes, 7 days is a perfect amount of time to experience the highlights of Southern Albania. By keeping daily drives under 2.5 hours, you can comfortably visit Berat, the Albanian Riviera, and Gjirokastër without feeling rushed.

faq.question: What is the best 7-day driving route from Tirana Airport to the Riviera?
faq.answer: The ideal loop goes from Tirana Airport to Berat (1 night), over the Llogara Pass to Himarë (1 night), down to Sarandë/Ksamil (2 nights), inland to Gjirokastër (1 night), and back to the airport via the main interior highway.

faq.question: Is driving through the Llogara Pass difficult for tourists?
faq.answer: The Llogara Pass is paved and well-maintained, but it is steep with sharp hairpin turns. It is not overly difficult if you take your time, use engine braking on the descent, and remain attentive to the spectacular coastal views.
